It explicitly forbids exposing secrets in reports and instructs conservative edits rather than wide data collection.

It does modify long-term memory (MEMORY.md) and today's journal (appending a log), which is consistent with its purpose but is a persistent change to agent state — users should expect and permit these file edits before enabling autonomous runs.

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but it will read and edit your agent's MEMORY.md and append logs to daily memory files. Before enabling automatic/cron runs: 1) make a backup of MEMORY.md (so you can undo unwanted edits), 2) run a manual, supervised consolidation first to inspect the report and edits, 3) ensure memory files don't contain unencrypted secrets (the skill will read them and is configured not to expose secrets but mistakes happen), and 4) if you install via the README's git/curl commands, verify the upstream repository URL is the one you expect. If you want tighter control, keep it user-invocable only (no cron) or run it in a sandboxed copy of your workspace until you’re comfortable with its behavior.
llm.findings: [no-code-instruction-only] expected: Scanner found no code files to analyze; this is expected for an instruction-only skill. The security surface is primarily what SKILL.md instructs the agent to do (read/write local memory files).
